title: Jam sessions in hotel lobbies and Art Tatum's after-hours places
summary: Jam sessions broke out in hotel lobbies. In Cleveland at Val's in the Alley and in Toledo at Noble's, Art Tatum kept a piano and beer and musicians gathered until daybreak.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Yeah. And it -- and that's everywhere you went that that happened, and we would -- we would, like we went to a town and ran into a couple of bands, and the guys would be in the hotel lobby, starting to talking about playing, and first thing you know you got a jam session going right in the lobby without the piano or anything, just everybody would start playing and --
What did the hotel people do?

Listen, everybody would expect it, I guess, in most places, you know, and then they used to play at a place in Cleveland called Val's and Audile. In the Alley. That's where Art Tatum used to go and play. And he -- when he got off from work in Cleveland -- in fact, I think Art was working there.
And we used to all congregate at Val's In the Alley and play with Art all night, you know.

Val's in the Alley. And we would go -- then in Toledo he played at a place called Noble's, and we used to go down there, and that's wasn't Toledo, and we used to go down to Noble's and jam with Art. Everywhere Art Tatum was you'd find a session, you know, and you got a piano session or a few horns and (inaudible) because everywhere -- every city in the United States where Art had, where he played, he always had a place afterwards, some bar or some joint wher e he rented a piano, or if they didn't have one, kept tune and kept the icebox full of Pabst Blue Ribbon Beer --
Uh-huh, he liked those beers, didn't he?
-- and he'd go there and stay until daybreak because he never went to bed until daybreak. And he'd go there and all -- and all of the piano players of that area would collect there.
